speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B infection with acute liver failure.

I have established the clinical picture of jaundice and agitation in a young male with high-risk sexual behavior and a history of stimulant use. The combination of subacute onset jaundice, agitation (likely hepatic encephalopathy), and risk factors for blood-borne pathogens strongly points to an acute viral hepatitis, specifically Hepatitis B or C. Given the severity (encephalopathy) and the specific risk factors, I suspect acute Hepatitis B.

Since I must now provide a diagnosis, I will proceed with this conclusion based on the available evidence.

**DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B with Hepatic Encephalopathy.**
